reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BitClub Network participation through paid mining plans while claiming passive or daily income of up to $2,000 and describing the opportunity as risk-free. It repeatedly asks viewers to register through a link and highlights referral-based percentages from participant purchases, alongside account screens showing balances, payout details, and reinvestment or payment tables.

citations.quote: there are several entry options, this is $ 500 thousand dollars 2000 dollars
shares it proportionally between all participants who bought the packets.
The person who has been invited automatically receives additional profit from his or her customer each after he or she gets the bonus.

opening.argument: The presentation uses promotional language, but its claims are framed as personal experience and reported results rather than a universal promise. The speaker identifies a specific participation date and describes what happened in his own account, including receiving 9.15 bitcoin over more than two years. That is materially different from proving that every viewer will earn the same amount. The video also presents the mining arrangement, equipment purchases, and payout calculations as matters for viewers to examine, while the available material does not establish that any particular return is guaranteed. Even the earnings discussion contains visibly uncertain wording about valuation, so a careful viewer should treat the figures as claims requiring independent verification, not as a certification of outcome.

citations.quote: I am in the project since November 19, 2014
during this time I took 9.15 bitcoin
every share works for 1000 days
today is worth around $42m $12m

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution characterizes promotional claims as established guarantees. But its quoted entry options and proportional sharing only show how the program is described; they do not establish that returns are guaranteed or that the presentation proves deception. The cited referral statement likewise describes a commission feature, not necessarily the entire purpose or operation of the offer. The opening also adds claims about a $2,000 daily income, risk-free participation, and registration that are not supported by its three cited excerpts.

citations.quote: shares it proportionally between all participants who bought the packets.
The person who has been invited automatically receives additional profit from his or her customer each after he or she gets the bonus.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The first-person figures are presented to persuade viewers to buy, not merely as neutral uncertainty: the speaker says the package payback is a little more than six months and calls the profitability real. The video also explicitly describes a risk-free business and daily earnings as high as $2,000. Those are substantive inducements, while the unclear valuation wording does not meaningfully warn viewers about risk or disprove the paid-mining return pitch.

citations.quote: if you want to earn $200 or even $2,000 daily
start your risk-free business from home
my payback of the package consists of a little more than 6 months

opening.argument: The video can reasonably be understood as a demonstration and explanation of how a cryptocurrency-mining service claims to work. It walks through entry options, equipment allocation, daily accounting, wallet activity, and the duration of a share. The account pages and wallet screens support that instructional format: viewers are shown operational interfaces rather than being asked to rely only on abstract promises. The narration explains that the company buys and updates mining equipment, allocates proceeds among participants, and can reinvest part of the proceeds in equipment. A presenter describing his own account and showing the site’s tables is consistent with a product walkthrough or personal review. That the presentation is favorable does not by itself turn an operational demonstration into proof of a scam.

citations.quote: The company updates the equipment for you. You don't need to worry about anything.
each day calculates the profit part of this profit, you can withdraw right away

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution focuses on the existence of paid plans, but a tutorial can explain a paid service without independently certifying it. The quoted proportional-sharing language describes the system’s stated mechanics, while the wallet, payout, and dated tables are precisely the operational material a demonstration would show. Referral compensation may be discussed as one feature without proving that the video’s central format is deceptive recruitment.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not neutral: it repeatedly connects the operational screens to purchasing and earning passive income. The narrator says the equipment purchase produces high profitability unavailable elsewhere, calls the arrangement a unique passive-income opportunity, and explains that invited customers generate additional profit. Showing interfaces does not verify that the balances represent real mining proceeds or that the service performs as claimed.

citations.quote: Buy equipment and get a high profitability from Bitcoin mining, which is not available today in the world for anyone.
you can build a true passive income
The person who has been invited automatically receives additional profit from his or her customer each after he or she gets the bonus.

opening.argument: At its most concrete, the video describes a paid service involving mining equipment, account administration, cryptocurrency balances, and a stated allocation of proceeds. That is ordinary commercial activity as presented: customers select packages, the company operates or updates equipment, and the account displays calculations and payout options. The available material does not show the creator requesting passwords, identity documents, or unrestricted deposits, nor does it establish that no mining equipment exists. It also does not prove that the referral feature is a downline scheme rather than a disclosed commission arrangement. The presence of prices, purchase options, and referral compensation may make the offer worth investigating, but those elements alone do not establish a scam mechanism or prove that the service is fictitious.

citations.quote: the company buys equipment for the mining of bitcoins
The company updates the equipment for you.
The person who has been invited automatically receives additional profit from his or her customer each after he or she gets the bonus.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s excerpts establish that packages and participant sharing are advertised, but advertising a paid mining service is not itself proof of fraud. The cited bonus statement shows disclosure of compensation, not concealment. Nothing in those excerpts establishes that the operator lacks equipment, that displayed balances are fabricated, or that viewers are required to provide credentials. The evidence therefore supports scrutiny of a commercial offer, not a conclusive scam finding.

citations.quote: shares it proportionally between all participants who bought the packets.
The person who has been invited automatically receives additional profit from his or her customer each after he or she gets the bonus.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing-credential point is beside the issue: a paid-mining scam does not require a password request in the video. The offer directly ties package purchases to mining returns, describes passive income accumulating daily, and presents referral payments from customers. The visible purchase screens and payout tables reinforce that viewers are being encouraged to buy an income-producing package, not merely shown an ordinary retail product.
